sources.text:
A scheduler chooses which ready job receives the processor. Turnaround time equals completion time minus arrival time. Response time equals the first time a job runs minus its arrival time. These metrics measure different things: early access to a processor does not necessarily imply early completion. First-come, first-served runs jobs in arrival order without preempting them. Shortest Job First selects the shortest available job and is non-preemptive. Shortest Time-to-Completion First is preemptive and selects the job with the least remaining processing time. Comparisons involving these shortest-job policies must state how execution lengths are known.

Round Robin rotates through a ready queue, running each selected job for at most one time slice before moving an unfinished job to the back. Shorter slices can improve initial responsiveness but increase the frequency of context switches. Larger slices amortize switching costs but can lengthen waits before a different job first runs. Neither a smaller average response time nor a smaller switching fraction alone establishes that a policy is best for every objective.

A multi-level feedback queue, or MLFQ, uses observed execution behavior instead of requiring exact future job lengths. Jobs in higher-priority queues run before lower-priority jobs; equal-priority jobs can share service by Round Robin. New jobs begin at high priority, and consuming the allowed CPU allotment causes demotion. Accounting for total consumed allotment prevents a job from retaining high priority indefinitely merely by yielding just before each slice ends. Periodic priority boosts can help jobs otherwise left waiting at low priority. Queue levels, slice lengths, allotments, and boost intervals are policy parameters, not universal constants.

This fixture adds an explicit scheduling model for exercises. It is authored example scaffolding rather than text copied from a textbook. Unless a question states otherwise, there is one processor, jobs are independent, and each job consists of one CPU burst with no I/O. Arrival times and required CPU service are provided. The processor never serves two jobs simultaneously. Time spent switching is not CPU service delivered to any job. A job that finishes before its slice ends does not use the remaining slice. If a job arrives at exactly a slice boundary, the question must say whether that arrival is enqueued before or after the preempted job. Ties must be resolved by an explicit rule, such as alphabetical job names.

A question that includes switching overhead must define when that overhead applies: for example, only when moving between different jobs, with no initial dispatch charge. It must also state whether arrivals can occur while switching and how they enter the queue. Questions that ignore overhead must say so. These conventions make a timeline reproducible and prevent a numeric answer from depending on unstated simulator behavior.

A comparison can report each job's first-run and completion times, then compute the requested averages. A design recommendation also needs an objective and constraints, such as a maximum response time, a switching budget, or a fairness requirement. A policy can satisfy one constraint while losing on another metric. Choosing a scheduler should therefore follow the stated workload and requirements. Hypothetical burst lengths and budgets introduced in an exercise are not measured workload traces, and labels assigned by the generator are not empirical student difficulty measurements.

sections.heading: Model and conventions for this item
sections.text: Use one processor with independent jobs, each having a single CPU burst and no I/O. Arrivals are in abstract time units: A at t=0 (burst 5), B at t=1 (burst 4), C at t=2 (burst 2). Ties and simultaneous arrivals follow the stated queue order; no id reordering is needed here. Switching cost applies only when the processor moves between different jobs, and the initial dispatch is free. During a switch, the next job is chosen first, and any job arriving during the switch interval is appended to the tail of the ready queue (during_switch = tail); a job arriving exactly at the end of a slice is enqueued after the unfinished, just-requeued job (boundary = after). A job that finishes before its slice ends releases the processor immediately, and a job that finishes in less than a full slice makes the following transition to a different job free (early_finish_free). Time spent switching delivers no service.

questions.stem:
A ready queue serves three independent, single-burst jobs (no I/O) on one processor: A arrives at t=0 with burst 5; B arrives at t=1 with burst 4; C arrives at t=2 with burst 2. Use Round Robin with sliding time slices. Conventions: the initial dispatch is free; switching cost c applies only when the processor moves between different jobs (continuation of the same job is free); the next job is selected before the switch begins, and a job arriving during a switch interval is appended to the tail of the ready queue; a job arriving exactly at the end of a slice is enqueued after the unfinished job that was just moved to the back; a job that finishes before its slice ends frees the processor immediately and makes the following transition to a different job free; switching time delivers no service to any job. Response time = first time a job runs minus its arrival time; turnaround time = completion time minus arrival time.

(a) With time slice q = 2 and switching cost c = 1, give the full execution timeline (run intervals for A, B, C and each switch interval).
(b) For the same q = 2, c = 1, give each job's response time and turnaround time, plus the average response time and average turnaround time.
(c) Find the average response time when the switch cost is removed (q = 2, c = 0) and when the slice is lengthened (q = 3, c = 1). Which of the three settings gives the smallest average response time, and how many switches does each setting use?
(d) A stated requirement is: average response time at most 2 time units AND at most 6 switch intervals. Decide which of the three settings (q=2,c=1), (q=2,c=0), (q=3,c=1) you would deploy, and justify the choice using both metrics.
questions.answer:
(a) Timeline for q = 2, c = 1: A runs 0-2 (used its full slice); switch 2-3; B runs 3-5 (full slice); switch 5-6; C runs 6-8 and finishes (burst 2, exactly its slice, so the 8-9 transition to A is not free); switch 8-9; A runs 9-11 (full slice); switch 11-12; B runs 12-14 and finishes (burst used 2 of its slice, so the next transition is free); A then runs 14-16 with no switch cost, finishing. So: A [0,2], [9,11], [14,16]; B [3,5], [12,14]; C [6,8]; switch intervals [2,3], [5,6], [8,9], [11,12] = 4 switch units, 5 switch intervals.
(b) q=2, c=1: A first runs at 0, completes at 16, so response 0, turnaround 16. B first runs at 3, completes at 14: response 2, turnaround 13. C first runs at 6, completes at 8: response 4, turnaround 6. Average response = (0+2+4)/3 = 2.0. Average turnaround = (16+13+6)/3 = 35/3 ≈ 11.67.
(c) q=2, c=0: A [0,2],[6,8],[10,11]; B [2,4],[8,10]; C [4,6]. (d) Only (q=2,c=0) satisfies the target of average response ≤ 2 (it gives 1.0) within the budget of at most 6 switches (it uses 5); (q=2,c=1) meets the switch budget (5) but misses the response target (2.0 is not ≤ 2 when the constraint is read strictly — under an inclusive reading it is only borderline and still no better than the alternative); (q=3,c=1) uses the fewest switches (4) but is worst on average response (3.0). Deterministic single-processor RR or STCF scheduling with independent, single-burst processes and no I/O. Times are integer abstract time units. Initial dispatch and dispatch after an idle interval are free. RR boundary=before/after orders arrivals exactly at a slice end before/after the unfinished process is requeued; earlier waiting processes keep their position. during_switch=tail appends switch-time arrivals to the queue; before_preempted inserts them immediately before the just-preempted process if it is still queued, otherwise at the tail. The next process is selected before switching, and arrivals through the switch end are enqueued before it starts. early_finish_free waives the next different-process switch cost only if the previous process completed in less than a full quantum. Same-process continuation is free. STCF supports zero switch cost only and chooses (remaining time, id), including id-based preemption on equal remaining times. Id comparison is Unicode lexicographic order. switch_count counts adjacent different-process transitions, including free early-finish transitions, but excludes initial/idle dispatch. makespan is final completion measured from time zero, including initial and intermediate idle intervals. Consecutive run intervals for the same process without an intervening switch/idle interval are merged.

Deterministic single-processor RR or STCF scheduling with independent, single-burst processes and no I/O. Times are integer abstract time units. Initial dispatch and dispatch after an idle interval are free. RR boundary=before/after orders arrivals exactly at a slice end before/after the unfinished process is requeued; earlier waiting processes keep their position. during_switch=tail appends switch-time arrivals to the queue; before_preempted inserts them immediately before the just-preempted process if it is still queued, otherwise at the tail. The next process is selected before switching, and arrivals through the switch end are enqueued before it starts. early_finish_free waives the next different-process switch cost only if the previous process completed in less than a full quantum. Same-process continuation is free. STCF supports zero switch cost only and chooses (remaining time, id), including id-based preemption on equal remaining times. Id comparison is Unicode lexicographic order. switch_count counts adjacent different-process transitions, including free early-finish transitions, but excludes initial/idle dispatch. makespan is final completion measured from time zero, including initial and intermediate idle intervals. Consecutive run intervals for the same process without an intervening switch/idle interval are merged.

function.name: mcp__teaching__cpu_schedule_v1
function.description:
Deterministic single-processor RR or STCF scheduling with independent, single-burst processes and no I/O. Times are integer abstract time units. Initial dispatch and dispatch after an idle interval are free. RR boundary=before/after orders arrivals exactly at a slice end before/after the unfinished process is requeued; earlier waiting processes keep their position. during_switch=tail appends switch-time arrivals to the queue; before_preempted inserts them immediately before the just-preempted process if it is still queued, otherwise at the tail. The next process is selected before switching, and arrivals through the switch end are enqueued before it starts. early_finish_free waives the next different-process switch cost only if the previous process completed in less than a full quantum. Same-process continuation is free. STCF supports zero switch cost only and chooses (remaining time, id), including id-based preemption on equal remaining times. Id comparison is Unicode lexicographic order. switch_count counts adjacent different-process transitions, including free early-finish transitions, but excludes initial/idle dispatch. makespan is final completion measured from time zero, including initial and intermediate idle intervals. Consecutive run intervals for the same process without an intervening switch/idle interval are merged.
